title: Minimum Addition to Make Integer Beautiful
summary: Given positive integers n and target, find the smallest non-negative integer x such that the sum of the digits of n + x is less than or equal to target.
statement: Given positive integers n and target, find the smallest non-negative integer x such that the sum of the digits of n + x is less than or equal to target. It is guaranteed that a solution always exists.
constraints: A number is beautiful when its decimal digit sum is at most target.
Return the smallest non-negative x such that n+x is beautiful.
reference_solution:
def minimum_beautiful_addition(n,target):
    original=n;place=1
    while sum(map(int,str(n)))>target:
        digit=(n//place)%10
        if digit:n+=(10-digit)*place
        place*=10
    return n-original

def minimum_beautiful_addition(n,target):
    original=n;place=1
    while sum(map(int,str(n)))>target:
        digit=(n//place)%10
        if digit:n+=(10-digit)*place
        place*=10
    return n
hints: While the digit sum is too large, inspect decimal places from right to left.
Round the current nonzero digit up to zero by adding (10-digit)*place, carrying into higher positions.
Continue until the digit sum meets target, then subtract the original n.
Any smaller addition than the first required rounding leaves the current suffix nonzero and cannot reduce the digit sum enough; successive forced roundings therefore give the minimum.

tests.explanation: Adding four reaches 20, whose digit sum is two; additions zero through three keep digit sum above six.
Adding 33 reaches 500 with digit sum five, while no smaller addition meets the target.
